  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section distinguishes between two aspects of Torah, charity, and communal prayer: one relating to the world and one relating to the person performing them.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2.</t>
    <t s="1">And to understand what is said, "All who engage, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="2">which speaks about a person who engages, and not about the matters of Torah, charity, and communal prayer themselves,</t>
    <t s="3">in the engagement of Torah, charity, and communal prayer,</t>
    <t s="4">which are the general three lines,</t>
    <t s="5">there are two matters: one—what pertains to the world,</t>
    <t s="6">that in the world the matters of the three lines should be actualized,</t>
    <t s="7">so that through this there will be a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower realms.</t>
    <t s="8">And the second—what pertains to the person who serves,</t>
    <t s="9">that he must do [his service] in these three matters.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section draws a parallel to eating holy offerings, which also has two aspects: a commandment upon the eater and a concern for the offerings themselves.</sectionSummaryBrief>

    <t s="8">(and in this matter, the conditions of anointing, etc., are not relevant).</t>
  </section>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the order of Torah, charity, and prayer is from lower to higher, with prayer being superior as an elevation.

translations.translation: But still, it must be said,
for the Torah is eternal.
From this it is forced that the order of these three matters in this maamar
is also applicable now.
And it can be explained according to what is explained elsewhere
that in elevation one can reach a higher level than in drawing down.
And accordingly,
prayer, which is an elevation from below upward,
its virtue is greater than that of Torah and charity.
And based on this, the order of these three matters will be understood even now,
that this order is from below upward: first—Torah,
then charity,
which
(now)
is above Torah,
and then prayer,
whose virtue is greater than the drawing down of Torah and charity,
as above.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between two aspects of Torah, charity, and communal prayer: one relating to the world and one relating to the person performing them.

translations.translation: And to understand what is said, "All who engage, etc.,"
which speaks about a person who engages, and not about the matters of Torah, charity, and communal prayer themselves,
in the engagement of Torah, charity, and communal prayer,
which are the general three lines,
there are two matters: one—what pertains to the world,
that in the world the matters of the three lines should be actualized,
so that through this there will be a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower realms.
And the second—what pertains to the person who serves,
that he must do [his service] in these three matters.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section draws a parallel to eating holy offerings, which also has two aspects: a commandment upon the eater and a concern for the offerings themselves.

translations.translation: (And analogous to what is in the eating of holy offerings, where there are two matters: one—it is a mitzvah to eat the sacrifice,
and this mitzvah is upon the person who eats,
and it has several conditions
(regarding anointing,
for greatness,
he is not liable).
The second—regarding the holy offerings themselves,
that they should not come to be leftover
(and in this matter, the conditions of anointing, etc., are not relevant).
